label: Record the screen
source: research/33-film-bible.md 10.2 (the skeleton) and 10.3 (this film's storyboard, voice and delivery columns verbatim); voice and chain from research/41-voice-and-pitch.md

sections.name: preroll
sections.note: the 2.000 s poster card: the pad and the logo mnemonic only. No kick, no bass, no hats, no plucks; the first hit is on the cut out of the card

sections.name: drive
sections.note: kick + bass + 16th hats enter on bar 3

sections.name: lift
sections.note: plucks up an octave, shimmer in

sections.name: out
sections.note: the end card: single hit on bar 8 beat 1, ring out. Two bars now: the card holds the spoken close, so the ring-out and the thinned hats carry the whole of it.

swells.note: reverse swell into the end card

outPlan.note: ringOut: the end card is a single bar here, so the thinned hats keep running under the single hit and the logo. Without it the master's gain takes the last ~0.5 s below -40 dBFS and the mix gate fails.

bed.padNote: the sustained band-limited chord, voiced two and three octaves above the plucks so it lives in 1-4 kHz - the band a voice rest sounds empty in - without touching the 20-200 Hz anti-engine band. Same layer and same gain as the commercial: without it these beds carried 4.5-4.9 % of their energy in 1-4 kHz against the commercial bed 25.5 %.

sfx.note: the mnemonic under the poster card; it does NOT shift with everything else, because the pre-roll bar would otherwise carry no sound at all
the cut into shot 2; the chip enters
the row is pressed in the panel
on the cut into the end card

voice.note: The commercial's final recipe: one Gemini request per line, one voice and one delivery instruction, the gate selecting by shot fit among contour-passing draws, the clean chain with a +6 dB bell at 3.9 kHz whose gain is inside the voice trim.

lines.why: the spoken close on a 4.25 s end card: anchored at the film end minus 4.25, which is the 13.75 it already sat on.
